speaker: thomas_hobbins
text: Six at the bridge. Not a quarter after. I don't hold a string for a man who is bidding his house goodbye by the inch.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Six. I'll be on the stones.

speaker: thomas_hobbins
text: Six horses, nose to tail, and the spare. The spare is for you as far as Shipston, and I'll hear no argument out of a back.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I can walk the first mile.

speaker: thomas_hobbins
text: You can walk it into a ditch and I'll still have put you up. Ten miles in the saddle, and you carry nothing. After Shipston you may be proud.

speaker: anne_shakespeare
text: He will be proud on the horse and sorry at the dismount. Let him have both.

speaker: thomas_hobbins
text: The pack's carriage, and the spare's saddle, two shillings. I'll have it at the Bell, not in your mother's kitchen.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Two shillings at the Bell. It's written, near enough.

speaker: richard_shakespeare
text: The pack is by the stair. I'll bring it down. Don't describe the knot.

speaker: thomas_hobbins
text: Gloves, a cheese, the town's letters, and you carrying none of it. A man with a back does not argue a pack onto his own shoulder.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Richard has it. I will not carry it, and I will not describe the knot.

speaker: anne_shakespeare
text: His back is not a parcel, Master Hobbins. If he slides, you stop.

speaker: thomas_hobbins
text: I stop for a thrown shoe. I'll stop for him. Two and a half miles in the hour, which is the horses', and it will suit a spine better than a hero.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I am not hiring a hero. I am hiring the spare.

speaker: thomas_hobbins
text: Then be at the bridge at six, and leave the farewell on this side of the door. I have had farewells that cost me a mile.

speaker: anne_shakespeare
text: He is packed already. The evening was going to arrange itself round him, and he would not wait for it.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: The inkhorn is not in the pack. I had it an hour ago.

speaker: richard_shakespeare
text: Then it is in the house. I'll not hunt a horn when the horses are in the dark.

speaker: thomas_hobbins
text: Find it before supper. A man may forget his lines. He'd best not forget his ink, if ink is his trade.

speaker: richard_shakespeare
text: I will look in the house. I will not look in the dark, and I will not look in the pack twice.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Once in the house, then. If it is not in the house, it can be a grievance after supper, and not before.

speaker: anne_shakespeare
text: It will not become a grievance if thou finds it. Go. The horses are his business. The horn is thine.

speaker: thomas_hobbins
text: Six horses, and the spare under you as far as Shipston. I have said it. I am not saying the road's length in a kitchen.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Six, at the bridge. The spare to Shipston. Two shillings at the Bell. I have those, and I am going after the horn.

speaker: richard_shakespeare
text: Then go. The pack will be where I said it would be, and the horn will not be in it.

speaker: anne_shakespeare
text: Go and look, Will. Master Hobbins has his six, and his two shillings, and his spare. Thou hast a horn to find.
